name: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!

info.desc: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo! is the debut studio album by the American new wave band Devo. It was originally released in August 1978, on the labels Warner Bros., and Virgin. Produced by Brian Eno, the album was recorded over a period of four months between October 1977 and February 1978, primarily in Cologne, Germany, The album received somewhat mixed reviews from critics and peaked at number 12 on the UK Albums Chart and number 78 on the U.S. Billboard chart. Recent reviews of the album have been more uniformly positive, and the album has charted .

podcast.body: This was the band's debut record, produced by Brian Eno in Germany. Its title references a line from H.G. Wells' 1896 book, *The Island of Dr. Moreau*, which explores the concept of surgically mashing humans and animals to "evolve" mankind, resulting in devolution. "That debut record was produced by Brian Eno in Germany."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Devo's 1978 debut album, featuring their distinctive sound and a cover of The Rolling Stones' "Satisfaction," served as an early, sometimes confusing, introduction to New Wave music for many listeners who had expected something akin to traditional punk bands. "I had read that they were weird and different, which made them a bit scary."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 1: New Wave

podcast.body: Devo's debut album, destined to "change history forever," was recorded with Brian Eno in the same studio in Berlin where David Bowie's "Heroes" was being made in 1977. Bowie had discovered the band in New York in 1976.

podcast.body: The title of Devo's album was adapted from a line in H.G. Wells' 1896 science fiction novel, "The Island of Dr. Moreau," reflecting the band's intellectual and sci-fi-bent approach to their music. "The album even adepts its title from a line in an 1896 science fiction novel called The Island of Dr. Moro."

podcast.body: The title of this album is famously adapted from a line in H.G. Wells' 1896 science fiction novel, "The Island of Dr. Moreau," reflecting Devo's intellectual and sci-fi-infused approach to their music. "The album even adeps its title from a line in an 1896 science fiction novel called The Island of Dr. Moro. Are we not men? The answer in this case is we are Devo."
